notes: Every advisory that survives `pnpm audit` needs a record here, and every
GHSA listed in pnpm-workspace.yaml auditConfig.ignoreGhsas needs a record
with `suppressed: true`. `pnpm audit:policy` enforces both directions and
fails once a record passes its recheckBy date, so an accepted risk cannot
moderate and low records below are therefore non-blocking, but they are
still tracked so the runtime graph stays auditable for downstream

accepted.introducedVia: @happyvertical/ai@0.106.0 -> @anthropic-ai/sdk@0.90.0; npm latest AI 0.107.0 also pins SDK 0.90.0 (rechecked 2026-10-24).
accepted.exploitability: The optional BetaLocalFilesystemMemoryTool persists files with unsafe default modes. Fresh searches of SMRT source and installed AI distribution found no import or construction of this helper or beta/tools/memory; the provider constructs ordinary Anthropic clients. Exposure requires a downstream consumer separately constructing the optional helper. Advisory: https://github.com/anthropics/anthropic-sdk-typescript/security/advisories/GHSA-p7fg-763f-g4gf
accepted.decision: Retain non-suppressed acceptance for the unconstructed optional tool rather than force an unvalidated 0.x SDK minor beneath the owning published AI package. An override is technically possible, but its provider compatibility has not been validated; the patched SDK already exists, so recheck in 30 days.
accepted.remediation: Request an @happyvertical/ai release adopting SDK >=0.91.1, then raise the catalog pin. Latest owner metadata: https://registry.npmjs.org/@happyvertical%2fai/latest . Reassess reachability and owner update by 2026-11-23.

accepted.introducedVia: Runtime parents bull@4.16.5 -> uuid@8.3.2; gaxios@6.7.1 and googleapis-common@7.2.0 -> uuid@9.0.1 (rechecked installed sources 2026-10-24).
accepted.exploitability: Only v3/v5/v6 with caller-provided undersized output buffers or large offsets are affected. All installed vulnerable parent calls are zero-argument v4(): bull queue/timer-manager, gaxios request IDs, and googleapis-common multipart boundaries. No affected function or caller buffer/offset is constructed on these edges. Advisory: https://github.com/uuidjs/uuid/security/advisories/GHSA-w5hq-g745-h8pq
accepted.decision: Retain non-suppressed acceptance for verified v4-only usage instead of crossing several owning packages' declared major ranges without validating their contracts. Patched uuid 11.1.1 does support named v4 through CommonJS; an override is plausible, not inherently incompatible. Bull latest still requires ^8.3.0, so newer Google packages alone do not clear the graph. Recheck in 30 days.
accepted.remediation: Prefer owner dependency updates, then adopt them here; otherwise validate a targeted uuid >=11.1.1 override across all three parents. Modern gaxios 8/google-auth-library 11 remove their uuid edges but cross additional parent majors. Metadata: https://registry.npmjs.org/uuid/11.1.1 and https://registry.npmjs.org/bull/latest . Reassess by 2026-11-23.

accepted.introducedVia: fast-glob@3.3.3 -> micromatch@4.0.8 -> braces. Declared as a prod dependency by @happyvertical/smrt-cli, smrt-core, smrt-scanner, smrt-playground and smrt-workbench (and reached through smrt-scanner by its dependents such as smrt-dev-mcp); devDependency only of ads, agents, analytics, chat, commerce, events, ledgers, places, profiles, projects, properties, sites and users.
accepted.exploitability: Stack exhaustion needs a glob PATTERN nested thousands of `{` levels deep (micromatch/braces#70); measured on Node 26.9, fast-glob.sync first throws RangeError at ~4,200-4,600 levels (8,500+ pattern characters). braces only ever parses patterns: fast-glob expands them through micromatch.braces (out/utils/pattern.js) and tests candidate paths against picomatch regexes, so file names on disk never reach braces (a path is bounded by NAME_MAX 255 / PATH_MAX 4096 anyway). Every runtime fast-glob call in packages/*/src takes its patterns from code constants or from the local developer's build/CLI configuration: cli utils/generator.ts, commands/schema-contract.ts, commands/json-validator.ts and discovery/manifest-discovery.ts use constants; cli loaders/npm-loader.ts interpolates the `smrt gnode` template short name typed by the operator (not a package export); scanner discovery.ts takes include/exclude from OxcScanner/ManifestBuilder options set by Vite plugin config or CLI constants (core reaches it via utils/scanner-module.ts; smrt-dev-mcp passes constants plus `<member dir>/**` excludes built from directories that exist in the local checkout); smrt-playground and smrt-workbench vite.ts/discovery.ts use constants or the Vite plugin `packagesPattern` option. None runs in a request handler, and no REST, generated MCP or other network input reaches a glob pattern. Worst case is a developer crashing their own build or CLI with their own config.
accepted.decision: No patched release exists: braces 3.0.3 is both the npm latest and the top of the affected range, and micromatch 4.0.8 / fast-glob 3.3.3 (both latest) still require it, so no override can clear it. Removing braces means replacing fast-glob in five published packages, which changes the scanner's bounded discovery semantics (#2275: dot, ignore space, followSymbolicLinks) and the CLI/Vite plugin file discovery; that is a contract-level change not justified for a path no untrusted input reaches.
accepted.remediation: Upstream: micromatch/braces#70 (open) with fix PR micromatch/braces#72 (open, unreleased). Drop this suppression once a patched braces ships and micromatch/fast-glob resolve to it; if upstream stalls past recheck, replace fast-glob with a braces-free glob engine under its own issue.

accepted.introducedVia: @happyvertical/smrt-content -> @happyvertical/documents / @happyvertical/spider -> crawlee -> got-scraping -> got -> cacheable-request -> http-cache-semantics. No SMRT package depends on got, cacheable-request or http-cache-semantics directly.
accepted.exploitability: Affects a SHARED cache built on CachePolicy: a client sending `Cache-Control: max-stale` is served another user's zero-lifetime entry (e.g. one carrying Set-Cookie). Verified not reachable in SMRT: (1) SMRT is never that cache; its only consumer is packages/content/src/contents.ts, which calls documents fetchDocument(url, { cacheDir }) as an outbound client. (2) fetchDocument passes no scraper/spider, so spider uses its default basic scraper and DomAdapter (undici `request`); the crawlee adapter chunk is only dynamically imported for `spider: 'crawlee'`, which no SMRT source selects. (3) Even on that path, got only builds a cacheable-request when `options.cache` is set (got/dist/source/core/index.js), its default is undefined, and neither got-scraping nor any @crawlee/* package sets it. Spider's own page cache (CacheManager over @happyvertical/cache) is URL-keyed and does not use http-cache-semantics.
accepted.decision: No patched release exists: 4.2.0 is both the npm latest and the top of the affected range, and cacheable-request 13.0.19 (latest) requires ^4.2.0, so no override can clear it. The crawlee/got graph belongs to @happyvertical/spider; removing it from SMRT would mean dropping document fetching from @happyvertical/smrt-content for a path SMRT neither loads nor configures.
accepted.remediation: Upstream: kornelski/http-cache-semantics#56 (open) with fix PR kornelski/http-cache-semantics#58 (open, unreleased). Drop this suppression once a patched release ships and cacheable-request resolves to it.
